# 合部金光明經

**ID:** T0664
**Volume:** T16
**Category:** 經集部類
**Original Category:** 經集部
**Byline:** 隋 寶貴合
**Dynasty:** 隋
**Date:** 597
**Juans:** 8
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T0664

## Contributors
- 寶貴 (A001927)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

T664 is an editorial composite, not a fresh translation: in eight fascicles and 24 chapters, it splices supplementary chapters from later partial renderings into the frame of [曇無讖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E7%84%A1%E8%AE%96)'s *[Jīnguāngmíng jīng 金光明經](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0301)* (T663). The work was assembled in 597 by [寶貴](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%B6%E8%B2%B4) (Bǎoguì), a śramaṇa of the Dà xīngshàn sì 大興善寺 in Cháng'ān, with editorial assistance from the polymath bibliographer [費長房](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B2%BB%E9%95%B7%E6%88%BF) Fèi Chángfáng (compiler of the *Lìdài sānbǎo jì* 歷代三寶記) and the philologist [彥琮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%A5%E7%90%AE) Yàncóng of the Rìyán sì 日嚴寺.

**Abstract**

T664 is best understood as the philological response to the perceived deficiencies of [曇無讖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E7%84%A1%E8%AE%96)'s shorter version: by inserting Paramārtha's four supplementary chapters and the Zhōu-period Jñānagupta's additional material along with the freshly recovered *Zhǔlèi pǐn* and the *Yínzhǔ tuóluóní pǐn*, it gave Sui Buddhists a more complete and liturgically more useful *Suvarṇaprabhāsa*. The composite remained a working text in the East Asian sangha for about a century, until it was in turn rendered redundant by [義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8)'s *[Jīnguāngmíng zuìshèngwáng jīng 金光明最勝王經](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0303)* (T665, 703) — a single translation of the long Sanskrit recension. Its main scholarly value today lies in its preservation of [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6)'s otherwise lost *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* fragments and of 寶貴's preface as a window onto the philological self-conception of the Sui translation bureau.
